findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored unencrypted at rest by default.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / no ACL set
findings.description: No ACL or aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults which may allow unintended public access.
This bucket stores sensitive ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects are unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration despite storing model artifacts, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook data is stored unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL (likely intended to be 'log-delivery-write'); this typo means the bucket will not have the intended access control applied, potentially causing log delivery failures or unintended default ACL behavior on a sensitive audit bucket.
A vendor roster file is uploaded to a bucket with no encryption configuration, resulting in cleartext storage at rest.
